Consult Summary:
- Acute onset left arm paralysis with left facial tingling, dysphagia, and speech difficulty; suspected acute stroke. Emergency ambulance arranged for hospital evaluation.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Woke ~1 hour before the call unable to move the left arm; painless and persistent.
- Associated symptoms: Left-sided facial tingling since onset; difficulty drinking/swallowing; speech harder/slower than usual.
- Pertinent negatives: No left leg symptoms; no arm pain; no hand discoloration; no coldness of the hand; no prior similar episodes; no observed facial asymmetry by patient; no awkward sleeping position or new bed.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Losartan (dose/route/frequency not documented); Amlodipine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Penicillin (reaction not documented).
- Family history: Father with heart disease (details not known). No other relevant family history reported.
- Social history: Lives alone. Former smoker. Alcohol: beers—few drinks on weekends and a couple during the week.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded (telephone consult).
- Examination findings: Not performed (telephone consult).

Impression:
- Suspected acute cerebrovascular event (possible ischemic stroke) given sudden unilateral arm weakness, facial paresthesia, dysphagia, and speech difficulty with onset approximately 1 hour prior to contact.

Plan:
- Emergency response: Ambulance called to patient’s home for immediate transport to emergency department.
- Pre-arrival instructions: Patient advised to unlock front door and sit in the hallway to ensure access; clinician remained on the line until EMS arrival.
- Hospital course communicated: Anticipated ED assessment with stroke team involvement to determine eligibility for acute stroke therapy.
- Safety: Patient informed this is an emergency requiring urgent evaluation; symptoms persisted and speech was reported to be worsening during the call.

Quality checks:
- Missing clinically expected elements: Exact onset time/last-known-well; blood glucose; complete neurologic exam (including facial droop assessment by clinician); vitals; anticoagulant/antiplatelet use; medication doses/frequencies; penicillin reaction details; full social history (current tobacco status details, quantified alcohol intake); past surgeries.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall with minor pauses/hesitations; no major audio issues.
